reply_text:
*I’d hold the merge.* Reviewed `http-retries` (`b04b610`) against `main` (`5f9be03`). Three findings:

1. *High — `timeoutMs: 0` no longer disables timeouts* — `src/http.js:11`
   Changing `??` to `||` replaces explicit zero with 10,000ms. The nightly export explicitly uses zero because it can take ten minutes, so it can now abort after ten seconds while awaiting the response. Confirmed: main schedules no timer; this branch schedules 10,000ms. Restore nullish defaulting and add a zero-timeout regression test.

2. *High — retries silently replay non-idempotent requests* — `src/http.js:30–33`
   Every method now retries by default, including POST. A server can commit a write and still return 500/503; replaying it can duplicate the operation. An in-memory reproduction invoked the POST handler three times with default settings. Restrict automatic retries to safe/idempotent operations; require explicit opt-in and replay guarantees for writes.

3. *Medium — discarded response bodies aren’t released* — `src/http.js:32–33`
   Before retrying, the client neither consumes nor cancels the previous response body. With real fetch against a local server returning unfinished 503 bodies, both discarded bodies remained open after all three attempts. During upstream failures this can tie up connections and stall pooled clients. Release each discarded body before retrying.

*Validation:* all three existing tests pass, but they don’t cover these cases. Ran additional read-only reproductions; no files changed.
